messages:
Alex Kim: Heads-up: planned runtime kernel + inference lib patch for Dedicated pools (US/EU). Change window: 2026-04-01 00:30–02:30 UTC. Need statuspage blurb + customer email draft. @Support Lead can you own the comms?
Support Lead: On it. Quick Q — are we doing a hard pin for any customers during rollout? We should call out Dedicated only. :thinking_face:
Priya Singh: We should pin busy customers to 1.4.2 during staged rollout. Upgrade path 1.4.2 -> 1.4.3. Canary already running in eu-canary. Monitoring + rollback hooks in place.
Morgan Lee: Confirmed: runtime 1.4.3 contains kernel fixes and a new KV-cache alignment change. Risk: small perf variance on long-context jobs. Recommend pin for Dedicated customers with >1000 TPS per pool.
Alex Kim: OK. Support Lead, please include pinning note and targeted customer list (we'll provide list). Also include statuspage incident with 'partial maintenance' wording.
deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment job #deploy-37821 created by @morgan. Canary start: 2026-03-31T23:45:00Z. Targets: eu-canary, us-canary. Rollout planned to dedicated pools after canary ok.
statusbot: Status page draft created: 'Maintenance - Dedicated inference runtime update (EU/US)'. Visibility: public.
Dan O'Neill: Canary started logs show intermittent OOM in model shard on long sequences. Small sample only. I'm pausing the canary and rolling back canary to 1.4.2 now.
Priya Singh: Thanks Dan — hold rollout. I'll gather logs and trace backend memory growth. If root cause isolated, we can continue; otherwise we keep pinned and reschedule.
Morgan Lee: Agree with pause. Also adding auto-fallback policy: if pod OOM > 3 within 10m, route traffic to compatible variant (quantized-1.4.2). I'll push policy change.
Alex Kim: Support Lead — we need a short statuspage update explaining the pause and expected ETA for next update. Keep message minimal: customer impact, affected regions, what we're doing, ETA for next update.
Support Lead: Drafting now. Proposed statuspage/snippet and customer email body below. Please review.
Support Lead: ```Statuspage snippet
Title: Maintenance paused — Dedicated runtime update (EU/US)
Impact: Some Dedicated clusters scheduled for an upgrade are paused after canary detected instability. Customers may see transient errors on long-context requests if attempting to upgrade.
What we're doing: Canary rollback to 1.4.2 and investigation underway. No action required by customers at this time.
ETA next update: +60 minutes.```
Support Lead: ```Customer email subject: Update: Dedicated runtime maintenance paused for investigation
Email body: Hi — we started a scheduled runtime update for Redwood Dedicated clusters in EU/US. Canary testing detected instability for long-context workloads, so we paused the rollout and reverted canary to the previous runtime (1.4.2). Investigations are in progress; we expect to share a follow-up in ~60 minutes. No action required from you. If you rely on long-context jobs and want an immediate pin, reply and we'll apply a targeted pin. Thanks, Redwood Support```
Priya Singh: +1. Add a short ops note for SEs: which customers are pinned and how to request pin removal.
Morgan Lee: Draft config snippet for ops to apply pins quickly: ```# runtime pin helper
apply_pin --customer <cust-id> --from 1.4.3 --to 1.4.2 --reason "post-canary-stability"```
Dan O'Neill: I'm attaching minimal log excerpt showing OOM pattern (truncated): ```
[03-31T23:46:12Z] shard-3 OOM after allocate 1.2GiB
[03-31T23:46:13Z] kv-cache resize triggered
[03-31T23:46:13Z] pod restart
```
Alex Kim: Good. Decision: pause global rollout, rollback canary, notify customers (support lead), prepare pinning ops runbook, and reschedule full rollout pending root cause. We will not move forward with 1.4.3 until analysis done.
Support Lead: I'll push the statuspage update now and send the customer email to affected Dedicated contacts (list from Morgan). I'll also add a note in the email about how to request an immediate pin.
statusbot: Status page updated at 2026-04-01T00:01:23Z — 'Maintenance paused'. Public incident link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-2026-04-01-001
Morgan Lee: I'll follow-up with a root cause thread in eng-runtime once logs parsed. If we have a small fix, we might retest canary in 2–4 hours.
Alex Kim: Thanks all. Keep this thread for any customer-facing copy changes. If Ops needs a faster pin API, ping me and I'll unblock approvals. :thumbsup:
